Position Overview

ASAP
The Role
Northeastern University London invites applications for a Post-doctoral Research Associate (PDRA) in Neuromorphic Accelerators to work with Professor Bipin Rajendran as part of the NeuroWare Neuromorphic Computing Hardware Semiconductor IKC.
The successful candidate will work on the design, implementation and validation of hardware accelerators for state-of-the-art AI models based on neuromorphic computing and In-Memory Computing (IMC) principles for applications in enterprise, IoT and Networked Systems.
Core duties include:
• Contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of neuromorphic and in-memory hardware accelerators for training and inference of state-of-the-art AI models.
• Develop algorithms, architectures, and hardware–software co-design methodologies for energy-efficient AI computation on neuromorphic and in-memory computing (IMC) platforms.
• Collaborate with cross-disciplinary teams spanning hardware design, AI/ML algorithms, information theory, and systems software to enable end-to-end system integration and validation.
• Publish high-quality research outcomes in leading journals and conferences in neuromorphic computing, AI hardware, and computer architecture.
• Support the supervision and mentoring of PhD and MSc students within the research group.
• Engage with industrial and academic collaborators to support joint research activities, technology transfer, and translational impact.
• Contribute to project management activities, including technical reporting, proposal development, and dissemination of research outcomes.
We particularly encourage applications from those belonging to groups underrepresented in UK higher education.
About the Institute
The Intelligent Networked Systems Institute (INSI) at NU London is a newly established transatlantic research hub focused on next-generation connectivity and intelligent computing and learning systems. The INSI London Hub acts as a bridge between the US and Europe, advancing interdisciplinary collaboration across continents. INSI is dedicated to addressing pressing challenges in telecommunications, artificial intelligence, quantum information, and information processing—all with the objective of creating a more efficient, connected, and secure world.
Person Specification Criteria
To undertake this role, the following should apply – should you not have the experience below, please do highlight where transferable skills would assist with you undertaking the role.
Qualifications
• PhD in Computer Science, Electronics or Computer Engineering or related quantitative field.
Key Criteria
• Strong publication record in neuromorphic hardware design demonstrated through publications in leading conferences and/or journals, with expertise extending beyond materials and device optimisation toward system- and architecture-level innovation.
• Experience in the simulation, implementation, and validation of large-scale machine learning models, including probabilistic, neuromorphic, Transformer, and/or state-space models.
• Experience with ASIC and/or FPGA design, hardware prototyping, and tapeout workflows for emerging AI hardware systems.
• Experience in hardware–software co-design approaches aimed at mitigating, exploiting, or adapting to the non-ideal effects and variability of nanoscale devices.
• Effective communication (oral and written) skills, ability to write research reports and papers in style accessible to academic audiences
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team on research programmes
Additional Information
Enquiries
Informal enquiries may be made to Professor Bipin Rajendran (b.rajendran@nulondon.ac.uk). However, all applications must be made in accordance with the application process specified.
Application Process
Applications must include a CV and covering letter of no more than one page that addresses the criteria for the role and includes names and contact information of up to three references. References will only be sought for short-listed candidates.
The panel will be shortlisting for this position on a rolling basis so please apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close this post before the closing date if we receive a large number of applications.
Participation in the equal opportunities section is encouraged, but voluntary.

Job Description:
Start date: 16 August 2027
Location: Broughton, North Wales
Duration: 12.5 months
Applications close on 20 November 2026!
We love your interest in joining Airbus! There is no limit on the number of positions you can apply for, however, please be aware that you can only progress in the selection process for one position at a time. We recommend reviewing all available opportunities and applying to those that best match your experience and aspirations.
AI Guidance: We know you might be thinking about using AI to help you in your application - before you do, please read our guidelines on the use of AI for recruitment at Airbus https://www.airbus.com/en/careers/faqs#using-ai-in-your-application.
Benefits:
Salary: £24,246
35 hours per week // Flexible working hours // Hybrid working options available depending on the role // Half day Fridays! // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
About us:
Located in North Wales, Airbus in Broughton is responsible for assembling wings for the entire family of Airbus commercial aircraft which includes the A320 Family, A330 Family and the A350 XWB. The wings are one of the most technically complex parts of the aircraft. They define the overall aerodynamic performance and are particularly important for securing excellent eco-efficient solutions.
For this internship you will be part of the Supply and Support business (ISS) where you will be working in challenging, dynamic and multifunctional teams. We are the department responsible for panel machining, treatments and also stringer machining and treatments. We take the raw aluminium billets and produce wing panels. All these components are built at the very beginning of the manufacturing process.
The internship will give a unique insight into this area that could be potential career paths within Airbus. The program is designed so that you get to experience the enablement of the manufacturing process as well as planning for future rate ramp ups, you will also gain project skills along with knowledge around the industry and operational exposure.
What you will be doing:

ig.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/ext_ig/job/ci.description_excerpt:
Job Title
Senior Journey Transformation Analyst
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your Team
• Journey Transformation owns the end-to-end journeys that clients and colleagues move through: onboarding, funding, trading, servicing, disputes and account closure on the client side, and the operational workflows that sit behind all of them.
Your role in the Team’s Success
• Our job is to find where those journeys break, prove what the breakage costs, and drive the fix through to a measured result.
• Digital servicing and conversational AI are one lever we pull. Process redesign, channel change, automation, system configuration, policy change and eliminating steps at source are others. The lever follows the diagnosis, never the reverse.
• You are the engine of that mission. You work out where friction and servicing demand are really coming from, build the evidence for what will remove them, and drive those changes through to delivery and proven results. Working directly alongside the Head of Journey Transformation in a small core team, you will help establish our journey intelligence capability from the ground up: the mapping standards, the diagnostic methods and the evidence bar the team is held to.
• Change runs down two routes. Some is delivered directly within Operations, through our servicing and contact centre technology estate - and you will own that end to end. Some belongs on the roadmaps of other teams, such as app and web product, platform APIs, marketing or compliance, and has to earn its place there on the strength of the evidence behind it - so you will build cases strong enough to do that, then carry them through the governance that prioritises them.
This is not a documentation role. The mandate is change shipped and results proven.
What success looks like
By the end of year one:
• A credible current-state picture exists across our priority journeys, client and operational, to a standard the business trusts and returns to.
• Journey improvement runs as an ongoing cycle rather than a series of projects: a pipeline that always holds the next evidenced opportunity and shipped changes that continue to be optimised against live performance.
• The first changes have delivered proven, sustained improvement against their baselines, with guardrails intact, so friction is genuinely removed rather than moved.
• Success is measured in client and business outcomes, not technology milestones, to an evidence standard Finance signs off without argument.
• Other teams bring their journey problems to us, because the cases we put on their roadmaps delivered for their objectives as well as ours.
What you’ll do:
Diagnose
• Map and analyse end-to-end journeys across both client experiences and internal operational workflows, producing current-state assessments in BPMN or equivalent notation, and quantifying friction through cost, manual effort, error and rework rates, compliance exposure and scalability constraints.
• Lead journey discovery: run deep-dive sessions with operational teams, advisors, team leaders and system owners, capturing qualitative pain points alongside quantitative impact.
• Drive contact and failure demand to root cause, using contact reason data, conversation analytics, operational MI, advisor insight and journey analysis - going beyond what clients ask about to why the journey made them ask.
Build the case
• Own the pipeline of journey improvement and cost-to-serve opportunities: identify, size, prioritise and sequence them into a delivery roadmap and a maintained backlog.
• Build the case for each change: baseline established before any forecast, benefits sized conservatively at marginal cost, delivery route identified, guardrails defined.
• Produce evidence-based business cases with clear ROI, risk assessment and competitive benchmarking, pitched in terms the receiving audience acts on, whether that is Operations, Finance, Product or Compliance.
Deliver
• Translate journey improvements into clear business requirements, functional specifications and user stories, with Jira tickets and traceability maintained from journey finding through to system change.
• Own delivery of in-remit changes end to end, from definition through build to live.
• Broker changes owned by other teams onto their roadmaps through agreed governance, with evidence and a clear articulation of the benefit to their objectives as well as ours.
Prove
• Own performance in life: track every shipped change against its baseline, confirm the improvement is real and sustained before any benefit is claimed, and feed live performance into the next iteration.
• Hold the quality bar. On client journeys, deflection counts only as resolution: repeat contact rates and journey CSAT operate as guardrails on every case. On operational journeys, the equivalent test is that work removed is work eliminated, not work displaced to another team.
• Work closely with the data team on measurement design, with finance partners on benefits realisation, and with frontline advisors and team leaders whose insight is a primary source.
• Operate with awareness of IG's regulatory context, including Consumer Duty outcomes, the needs of vulnerable clients and the demands of a multi-jurisdictional operating model.
What You'll Need:
You can take a messy, real-world journey - client-facing or back-office - and turn it into a clear logical map with a defensible number attached to the friction, then carry the fix through delivery and stand behind the result afterwards.
Diagnostic craft
• Strong experience mapping end-to-end journeys across both customer-facing and operational processes, using BPMN or equivalent notation and tools such as Visio, Lucidchart or Miro.
• Proven ability to run stakeholder interviews and discovery sessions, asking detailed questions about how work actually happens and getting to the answer underneath the first one.
• A data-led approach to root cause: comfortable in contact and operational analytics, and in designing the measurement that will later prove the change worked.
Evidence and outcome ownership
• You establish a baseline before you forecast, size benefits conservatively, and have had your numbers challenged by finance or governance partners and defended them.
• You have owned an improvement outcome through to a measured result, and can speak precisely to the baseline, what landed and how it was…

This is a technical, delivery-focused role. Although the position carries a manager title, you’ll be directly involved in preparing and reconciling tax provisions, supporting the consolidation process and responding to audit requirements. You won’t simply coordinate work or oversee its completion. You’ll personally deliver key elements of the tax reporting cycle.
This is an excellent opportunity to broaden your international tax experience while working within a collaborative global tax function.
What You’ll Do
• Prepare group and statutory tax provisions for financial statement reporting and audits.
• Perform the underlying calculations and reconciliations required to support accurate tax provisions.
• Support the consolidation of tax information from multiple jurisdictions into the group reporting process.
• Prepare supporting schedules, analysis and documentation for internal and external audit requirements.
• Investigate and resolve differences identified through tax provision reconciliations.
• Act as a key contact for direct tax matters across assigned jurisdictions.
• Coordinate with local finance teams and outsourced service providers to support tax compliance obligations.
• Work with external advisers and tax authorities to support tax audits and manage tax risks.
• Assess the accounting impact of relevant tax and regulatory changes.
• Maintain and improve tax reporting processes, controls and supporting documentation.
• Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise or automate tax processes.
• Collaborate with colleagues across Tax, Finance, Legal, Operations and IT.
• Manage competing deliverables across jurisdictions while maintaining clear communication around progress, risks and deadlines.
What We’re Looking For
• A professional qualification such as ACA, ACCA, CTA, CPA or an equivalent accounting or tax qualification.
• Practical experience preparing tax provisions rather than only reviewing or overseeing work completed by others.
• Experience working with tax reconciliations and supporting tax reporting cycles.
• Knowledge of IAS 12 and/or ASC 740 tax accounting principles.
• Experience supporting financial statement audits and responding to audit queries.
• Understanding of direct tax compliance and its interaction with tax accounting and financial reporting.
• Experience working within a multinational organisation, professional services firm or similarly complex international environment.
• Strong analytical skills and confidence working with detailed financial and tax data.
• Experience using Excel and familiarity with ERP platforms such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite or comparable systems.
• Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively with stakeholders across functions and jurisdictions.
• A proactive approach to managing priorities, resolving issues and meeting reporting deadlines.
What Will Help You Succeed
You’ll enjoy working with the detail and taking personal ownership of technical deliverables. You’ll be comfortable preparing calculations, completing reconciliations, investigating differences and ensuring that your work is accurate and appropriately supported.
You’ll also know when to ask questions, obtain information from others and communicate early when a deadline, dependency or risk requires attention. This role will suit someone who wants to remain close to the technical work while continuing to develop their experience within a global tax environment.
Why Join Us?
You’ll gain broad exposure to group tax reporting across multiple jurisdictions and work closely with colleagues throughout a global organisation. The role offers the opportunity to deepen your expertise in tax provisioning, reporting, compliance, controls and process improvement while making a visible contribution to the Group Tax function.

Job Description
Purpose of the role
To develop, implement, and maintain an effective resilience strategy and Operational Recovery Planning and Incident Management framework aligned to industry leading standards and controls and regulatory expectations, to enable the bank to respond and recover important business services to severe but plausible scenarios, and minimise the impact to customers, clients, colleagues and the wider market.
Accountabilities
• Socialisation and implementation of the resilience strategy and underpinning framework across the firm (e.g. SMRs and delegates, business / function resilience role owners and all colleagues), ensuring compliance to the standard and controls.
• Development and enhancement of the resilience, crisis and incident management framework to uplift recovery and response capabilities to ensure Important Business Services can continue to operate during disruption events to minimise the impact on customers, clients and the market.
• Operational Recovery Planning and Security Incident Management planning standards and controls enhancement according to industry practice, emerging threats and regulatory requirements.
• Provide oversight to the business and technology recovery capability improvements, and uplifts to third-party (suppliers and Financial Market Infrastructure) recovery capabilities to enable Important Business Services to remain within or mitigate impact tolerance thresholds.
• Communication of the firm’s / business’ resilience position (risks and remediation) through clear and transparent scorecards / dashboards to enable effective investment decisions to the Board and Executive Committees, Control Forums and business stakeholders.
• Enhancement of resilience, crisis management and incident response and recovery capability through sophisticated, regular and adequate testing coverage to demonstrate Important Business Services’ ability to recover within impact tolerance for a severe but plausible scenario.
• Assurance that services and products are built resiliently by the business through the change management process (NAPAs, DRAs, material change process).
• Continually remain abreast of resilience and crisis and incident management developments, regulatory policy requirements and the emerging landscape.
• Mitigation of the impact of unexpected incidents by identifying, responding to and enabling the resolution of events that threaten the services, operations, infrastructure, colleagues and clients of the bank.
• Execution of responses to reported incidents and potential threats from various channels including intelligence, email, phone and monitoring systems prioritised by the assessed or actual impact to the bank.
• Documentation and analysis of past prioritised incident details, the steps to resolution and the lessons learnt to support the identification and implementation of preventative measures and process improvements.
Vice President Expectations
• To contribute or set strategy, drive requirements and make recommendations for change. Plan resources, budgets, and policies; manage and maintain policies / processes; deliver continuous improvements and escalate breaches of policies / procedures.
• If managing a team, they define jobs and responsibilities, planning for the department’s future needs and operations, counselling employees on performance and contributing to employee pay decisions / changes. The four LEAD behaviours are: L – Listen and be authentic, E – Energise and inspire, A – Align across the enterprise, D – Develop others.
• OR for an individual contributor, they will be a subject matter expert within own discipline and will guide technical direction. They will lead collaborative, multi-year assignments and guide team members through structured assignments, identify the need for the inclusion of other areas of specialisation to complete assignments. They will train, guide and coach less experienced specialists and provide information affecting long term profits, organisational risks and strategic decisions.
• Advise key stakeholders, including functional leadership teams and senior management on functional and cross functional areas of impact and alignment.
• Manage and mitigate risks through assessment, in support of the control and governance agenda.
• Demonstrate leadership and accountability for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work your team does.
• Demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the organisation functions to contribute to achieving the goals of the business.
• Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategies.
• Create solutions based on sophisticated analytical thought comparing and selecting complex alternatives. In-depth analysis with interpretative thinking will be required to define problems and develop innovative solutions.
• Adopt and include the outcomes of extensive research in problem solving processes.
• Seek out, build and maintain trusting relationships and partnerships with internal and external stakeholders in order to accomplish key business objectives, using influencing and negotiating skills to achieve outcomes.
All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset – to Empower, Challenge and Drive – the operating manual for how we behave.
Join Barclays as a Technology Resilience Lead within the Tesco Resilience team. This role is responsible for technology resilience capabilities, including the implementation of resilience controls, embedding resilience-by-design principles, and partnering with change and architecture teams to ensure resilience considerations are integrated into technology initiatives from the outset. Service and technical support
• Provide responsive on-site and remote support for incidents and service requests, taking ownership through resolution or effective escalation.

• Identify recurring issues and improvement opportunities, using data, customer feedback and root-cause analysis to strengthen service quality.

Essential experience and knowledge
• 5 – 10 years’ progressive IT support experience, including substantial 2nd-line work and exposure to 3rd-line or infrastructure activities.·
• Proven delivery of high-quality support to enterprise users, both in person and remotely, with ownership of complex incidents.·
• Strong Windows 10/11, Microsoft 365, Active Directory, Group Policy and Microsoft Entra ID knowledge.·
• Practical understanding of endpoint management, application deployment, patching and device compliance.·
• Sound networking knowledge, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, Wi-Fi, VPN and basic firewall concepts.·
• Working knowledge of Windows Server, virtualisation, file services, permissions and backup monitoring.
• Experience with an ITSM platform such as ServiceNow and disciplined use of incident, request, change and knowledge processes.

• CAD, time and attendance, environmental monitoring or operational/manufacturing technology support.
• SOX controls, vulnerability remediation, Cyber Essentials or comparable compliance activity.
• PowerShell scripting, awareness of Microsoft Azure or similar cloud services.
• Mentoring or coaching colleagues and contributing to continual service improvement.

Calm, accountable and service-focused, with clear written and verbal communication.
•
Proactive and self-directed, while collaborating effectively within a virtual, multi-disciplinary IT team.
•
Highly organised, able to balance planned project work with changing operational priorities.
•
Curious and adaptable, with a commitment to continuous learning and safe working.

Preferred

Security Clearance
At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.

Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. As Estates Facilities Manager, you will lead the hands-on delivery of facilities and maintenance services across your assigned properties and estates , managing the on-site estates and maintenance technicians and ensuring technical services are safe, compliant, cost-effective and aligned with Greystar's operational and resident/occupier service standards. This is a role you will be required to coordinate the wider technical delivery team, allocating tasks and taking personal responsibility for more complex or time-sensitive work. You are accountable for day-to-day estate operations, facilities and maintenance management, operational budgets, contractor management, planned maintenance delivery and operational reporting, escalating portfolio strategy, service charge governance, major procurement, capital planning and business planning matters to the Senior Commercial and Estates Manager. Estate Operations & Team Management

• Complete monthly financial reports and attend monthly finance meetings.
Contractor Management
• Manage contractors on-site day-to-day, ensuring RAMS, permits, and compliance measures are fully in place, and issuing permits to work as required.
• Coordinate and verify the quality of outsourced services and escalate issues as needed.

Alongside your day-to-day role, you will complete the Level 2 Bicycle Mechanic Apprenticeship (ST0622). Your formal apprenticeship training is included and combines workplace learning, online study, coaching and two short block-release technical courses. The programme normally lasts 18 months, followed by up to three months for the End Point Assessment. Successful completion leads to industry-recognised Cytech training and accreditation.
You do not need to be an experienced mechanic. We are looking for someone who is curious, practical and keen to learn, with a genuine interest in bikes, quality and how things work.
Key Responsibilities
Learning the Craft
•  Work alongside experienced bike mechanics to build confidence in bicycle inspection, servicing, repair and maintenance.
•  Learn to diagnose faults accurately and complete work using the correct tools, methods and technical information.
•  Develop practical capability across complete bike servicing, wheel building and bike preparation.
•  Build a strong understanding of Brompton products, components and quality standards.
•  Ask questions, seek feedback and apply learning to improve the quality and efficiency of your work.
Workshop Delivery
•  Support the safe and efficient flow of work through the workshop, completing assigned tasks carefully and on time.
•  Check your work thoroughly and raise any concerns, faults or quality issues with your manager or mentor.
•  Use, maintain and store tools and equipment correctly, keeping work areas clean, organised and safe.
•  Follow all health and safety, workshop and quality procedures, including the correct handling of bicycles, parts and materials.
•  Maintain accurate job, service and training records as required.
•  Treat every bicycle with care and contribute to a positive, supportive and high-performing team environment.
Customer & Product Experience
•  Learn how to explain completed work clearly and provide a professional bike handover.
•  Build confidence communicating with colleagues and, where relevant, customers about repairs, maintenance and bike care.
•  Represent Brompton's commitment to quality, craftsmanship and a brilliant customer experience in every task.
Your Apprenticeship
•  Take an active role in all elements of the apprenticeship, including workplace coaching, online learning, coursework, practical assessments and technical training.
•  Complete a minimum of six hours of off-the-job training each week during the 18-month programme, supported within your working hours.
•  Attend the two required block-release Cytech courses at one of the training provider's workshops.
•  Work towards Cytech Technical Two and Cytech Technical Three as part of the apprenticeship.
•  Keep your learning portfolio and evidence up to date, and prepare for the independent End Point Assessment.
•  Successfully complete the End Point Assessment, which includes an observed full bike service, an observed wheel build, a customer service and bike handover role play, and an interview based on portfolio evidence and coursework.
Skills
•  Practical Learning - Enjoys hands-on work and can apply instructions, demonstrations and feedback to build new skills.
•  Quality & Attention to Detail - Works carefully, checks their work and takes pride in getting the details right.
•  Problem Solving - Approaches faults logically, stays curious and is willing to investigate how things work.
•  Organisation & Reliability - Arrives prepared, manages learning and work commitments, and completes agreed tasks on time.
•  Communication & Teamwork - Listens well, asks for help when needed and contributes positively to the team.
•  Safety & Responsibility - Understands the importance of following workshop, quality and health and safety procedures.
•  Continuous Improvement - Welcomes feedback and looks for practical ways to develop their skills and improve their work.
•  Customer Focus - Understands that careful technical work and clear communication shape the customer's experience of Brompton.
What You'll Bring
•  A genuine interest in bicycles, mechanics, engineering or practical problem solving.
•  Motivation to complete a structured apprenticeship and build a long-term career in bicycle mechanics.
•  A careful, responsible approach and willingness to follow technical and safety instructions.
•  A positive attitude, curiosity and confidence to ask questions and learn from others.
•  The ability to work collaboratively and communicate clearly.
•  Commitment to working onsite in Greenford in a practical workshop environment.
•  Eligibility for the apprenticeship, including working in England and meeting the training provider's initial assessment requirements in maths and English.
•  No previous professional bike mechanic experience is required. Relevant practical experience, whether through study, work, volunteering or personal projects, would be helpful but is not essential.
What Success Looks Like
•  You make steady progress through your apprenticeship and complete learning activities and evidence on time.
•  Your practical confidence grows, allowing you to complete an increasing range of service and repair tasks safely and accurately.
•  Your work meets Brompton's expectations for care, quality and attention to detail.
•  You use feedback positively and take increasing ownership of your development and day-to-day work.
•  You contribute to a clean, safe, organised and supportive workshop.
•  You successfully complete the apprenticeship and End Point Assessment, building a strong foundation for a career as a qualified bike mechanic.

Atelier Ten is an international environmental design and building services consultancy and lighting design firm creating high-performance, sustainable, award-winning buildings. Our projects give back to the wider environment, conserve resources and foster innovation. Our London office has an immediate opening for a full-time Associate Director as part of our integrated team of environmental designers.
In this role, your overarching goal will be to support Atelier Ten’s continued success as we cover a wide range of building services engineering disciplines and provide cutting-edge sustainability and environmental design consultancy.
As an Energy Analyst who loves architecture and building science, you will be responsible for delivering environmental and sustainability advice on projects for both internal teams and external collaborators and clients. This will involve consulting on sustainability, environmental design, compliance with building regulations, thermal comfort, measurable operational energy use reduction, and design and delivery of net zero carbon and net zero energy buildings. Your consultancy will be demonstrated through sound analytics using a suite of analytical and computer science tools such as IES-VE, Rhino and grasshopper, EnergyPlus, Open Studio, Design Builder, MS Excel and bespoke, typically python-based, analysis tools.

• Critically review energy use, operational carbon, and thermal comfort related deliverables developed by others by managing initial framing and final review of analytical work across projects. This ensures:
• cross-cutting diagnosis of existing workflows and skill-shortages

A key part of the role involves managing and fine-tuning security monitoring tools such as SIEM platforms to ensure optimal visibility and threat detection. The Security Operations Manager collaborates with IT, infrastructure, and platform teams to coordinate responses to vulnerabilities and ensure swift resolution of incidents.
They also maintain and regularly test incident response plans, being central to simulation exercises to ensure readiness.
This role demands a high level of technical expertise, leadership, and the ability to remain calm and decisive under pressure. The Security Operations Manager is the frontline defender of the organisation’s cyber resilience, ensuring that threats are swiftly neutralised and that the business can operate securely and with confidence.
What you’ll be doing
As our Cyber Security Operations Manager, you’ll be at the forefront of safeguarding Anglian Water’s digital infrastructure — ensuring our systems, data, and services remain protected against evolving cyber threats.
You’ll:
•
Lead and manage our outsourced Security Operations Centre (SOC) provider, ensuring high performance, continuous improvement, and alignment with business priorities.
•
Oversee real-time threat detection, triage, and response — driving swift, effective action when incidents occur.
•
Own and maintain the organisation’s Cyber Incident Response Plan, coordinating major incident responses and ensuring lessons learned translate into stronger defences.
•
Manage and optimise key technical controls, including SIEM, SOAR, PKI, and email security tools, to maintain robust detection and response capabilities.
•
Collaborate with delivery partners and internal teams to improve service quality, mitigate risks, and enhance security posture.
•
Drive the continuous maturity and modernisation of our detective controls and SOC operations, ensuring alignment with the NIST framework.
•
Provide clear reporting and insights to senior stakeholders, ensuring informed decisions and proactive risk management.
As a valued employee, you’ll be entitled to:
•
Full private healthcare with no excess
•
26 days leave, rising with service + Bank Holidays, with the option to swap Christmas and Easter holidays for those celebrated by your religion
•
A flexible working culture
•
Competitive pension scheme – we double-match your contributions up to 6%
•
Life Assurance at eight times your salary
•
Personal Accident cover – up to 5x your salary
•
Bonus Scheme
What does it take to be the Cyber Security Operations Manager
You’ll be a calm, confident leader with excellent interpersonal and communication skills — someone who thrives under pressure and brings clarity and composure to complex situations.
You’ll have a strong people leadership style, capable of guiding teams and partners with empathy, direction, and accountability. With your deep problem-solving skills and pragmatic mindset, you’ll find balanced, effective solutions in fast-moving or high-stakes environments.
You’ll also be skilled at translating technical concepts into plain English, making complex issues clear and actionable for senior leaders and stakeholders. Confident in managing conflict and competing priorities, you’ll foster collaboration and maintain focus on achieving the best outcomes for the organisation.
Skills and Qualifications:
•
Qualified to Degree level or equivalent
•
Technical qualifications such as CISM, CISSP, CIPPE,CCSP, GICSP
•
Experienced in SecOps
•
Relationship building with team, colleagues, internal customers and external suppliers
•
Significant experience in Security Operations and Incident Response
•
Broad technical competence in IT and Cyber
•
Broad technical competence in OT
•
Solid understanding of SIEM/SOAR especially Sentinel
Why Apply?
At Anglian Water, we play a vital role in safeguarding one of life’s most essential resources — and protecting the systems that keep it flowing is critical to our mission. As our Security Operations Manager, you’ll be at the heart of that protection, leading the defence of our digital infrastructure that underpins services for millions of customers every day.
You’ll have the opportunity to shape how we detect, respond to, and recover from cyber threats — influencing strategic decisions and driving continuous improvement across our security landscape.
In return, you’ll join a forward-thinking, inclusive organisation that values innovation, personal growth, and work-life balance. You’ll work alongside passionate professionals, gain exposure to cutting-edge technology, and make a genuine difference in protecting essential services that communities rely on.

Convatec is entering an exciting new phase of its R&D journey with plans to establish a new state-of-the art facility in Manchester. The facility will strengthen collaboration with Manchester's world-class life sciences ecosystem and support our mission of pioneering trusted medical solutions to improve the lives we touch. This move will create exciting opportunities to help shape the future of healthcare innovation at Convatec.

The Analytical Laboratory Manager provides technical and analytical development support to Science & Innovation pipeline projects. You will lead the Analytical Laboratory testing programme, ensuring effective planning, prioritisation, coordination and execution of testing, method development and validation activities in accordance with internal procedures, applicable regulations and guidelines, and industry best practice. You will also lead and develop the Analytical team, maintain safety and quality compliance, deliver agreed key performance indicators, assure accurate technical documentation and work cross-functionally with project teams, Quality functions, manufacturing sites and other laboratory leaders to manage priorities, timelines and technical challenges.

Laboratory leadership and people management
• Lead, engage and communicate effectively with the Analytical team, including recruitment, employee development, coaching and performance management.
• Set clear expectations, provide guidance and identify development and training needs.
• Monitor team performance and delivery against agreed key performance indicators and drive continuous improvement.
Testing programme and technical delivery
• Manage, prioritise and oversee the analytical testing programme, including planning, coordination and execution of testing.
• Provide technical and analytical development support to Technology & Innovation pipeline projects.
• Define and execute strategies for analytical method development, validation and transfer, including validation in accordance with relevant ICH guidelines.
• Provide technical guidance for research, troubleshooting and manufacturing support activities.
• Keep abreast of scientific literature, emerging technologies and alternative ways of working.
Quality, compliance and documentation
• Ensure methods and validation activities comply with internal procedures, applicable regulations and guidelines, and industry best practice.
• Ensure accurate, timely review and approval of analytical and technical documentation, including testing and validation protocols and reports, technical reports, standard operating procedures and related controlled documents.

• Contribute as a functional laboratory leader to Design and Development projects conducted under Design Controls.

• Ensure appropriate risk assessments, safe systems of work and Control of Substances Hazardous to Health assessments are in place.

• Manage the departmental budget, including accurate budget setting and expense management.
• Manage relationships with suppliers of analytical equipment, software and services.

• Proven management experience leading and developing a team of scientists.
• Working knowledge of FDA and European quality-system regulations relevant to medical devices or pharmaceuticals.
• Knowledge of drug-device combination product technologies is preferred.
• Sound understanding of product development processes and Design Controls.
• Experience planning and executing analytical method validation and method transfer activities.
• Competence in the use, calibration and maintenance of advanced analytical laboratory equipment.
• Experience with computerised laboratory systems used to manage data and information, such as a Laboratory Information Management System.
• Ability to manage competing priorities, solve problems, identify inefficiencies and implement practical improvements.
• Strong cross-functional communication, collaboration, coaching and stakeholder-management skills.
• Effective technical writing, review and approval skills.
• Competence in preparing risk assessments, safe systems of work and Control of Substances Hazardous to Health assessments.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

• From early 2028, this position is expected to transition to our Manchester site, on a hybrid working model.

• Maintain project documentation, action logs, decision records, and governance materials.

• Support sales best practice initiatives and contribute to the maintenance of sales methodologies, documentation, and governance standards.
• Participate in strategic planning activities with Sales Managers and broader business stakeholders.
• Foster strong working relationships across global business units, product teams, and support functions.
• Support regulatory, compliance, audit, and other business-critical projects as required.

• Strong project management and coordination skills with the ability to manage complex, multi-workstream initiatives.
• Ability to build and maintain effective relationships across a diverse stakeholder group.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including presentation and facilitation capabilities.
• Commercial awareness and understanding of business development processes.
• Ability to assess and manage project risks, issues, and dependencies.
• Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise competing deadlines.
• Analytical and problem-solving capabilities with a focus on delivering practical solutions.

• Experience working within governance and control frameworks.
• Ability to coordinate teams and stakeholders across multiple locations and time zones.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively within cross-functional teams.

• Knowledge of financial services products, operations, and client servicing models.

• Experience managing large, complex, cross-functional projects involving multiple stakeholder groups.
• Experience supporting RFP, proposal, due diligence, or sales processes.
• Knowledge of investment operations, client servicing, and financial products.
• Experience working with geographically dispersed teams and global stakeholders.
• Understanding of governance, operational risk, compliance, and regulatory requirements within financial services.
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities within a fast-paced environment.

To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The SPTS division provides advanced wafer processing solutions—including etch, deposition and vapor-based technologies—designed for R&D through high-volume production. With a global presence and strong customer support network, SPTS helps manufacturers across industries improve performance, yield and cost-efficiency. It also offers comprehensive service and spare parts through a worldwide network of service centers and qualified local agents.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
Part of the KLA Engineering division, the Platform Engineering and Development Group delivers automation solutions that integrate KLA process systems into semiconductor fabs worldwide.
This new role offers exposure to emerging technologies and varied projects, including international travel to support product installations and customer applications.
We are seeking an experienced multidisciplinary engineer with strong electrical, electronic, and mechanical knowledge to support system operation, integration, calibration, diagnostics, Alpha/Beta systems, and retrofit activities, while providing design feedback and improvement recommendations.
You will work with specialists on equipment design and integration, delivering to tight deadlines in a highly regulated industry.
We will seek to give as much notice as possible for travel, but trips may be at very short notice and can be for up to 4 weeks at a time.  One-week visits would be more typical.  Weekend travel to site maybe required.
KLA will provide travel expenses and accommodation, in line with our travel policy.
Key Responsibilities:
• Maintain development and continuous improvement of Platform semiconductor handling hardware.
• Support new hardware designs through build, integration, fault-finding, and PLC readiness.
• Lead installation, commissioning, and technical resolution of new products at customer sites.
• Travel internationally up to 50% to support critical customer engagements and resolve complex technical issues.
• Translate customer requirements and factory learnings into business-critical design improvements.
• Shape technical responses to customer specifications and system-level requirements.
• Define robust design specifications that align customer needs, product strategy, and engineering standards.
• Champion serviceability, reliability, and maintainability in new product designs.
• Ensure machine performance and compliance against relevant international standards.
• Produce clear technical reports that support decision-making, risk management, and customer confidence.
• Lead hardware test strategy, validation planning, and performance characterisation.
• Produce support documentation and procedures.
• Influence cross-functional teams to optimise hardware performance, reliability, and customer readiness.
Key Skills Required
• A flexible work ethic and ability to use initiative
• Excellent analytical and fault-finding skills
• Able to work both autonomously and as part of a team
• Well organised – You’ll work autonomously, often in different time zones and be trusted to work without assistance or management.
• Composed – You’ll thrive in the sometimes-pressurised environment of semiconductor manufacturing environments.
• Able to demonstrate strong Communication skills – You’ll enjoy establishing and maintaining good working relationships with both customers and colleagues.
• Languages: Fluent English (Both written and spoken)
• Driving license to be able to travel throughout Europe
Occasional domestic and international travel, including to the United States, may be required as part of this role
What we will offer you?
Our benefits package includes:
Annual leave starting at 25 days (plus bank holidays), contributory pension scheme, cash health plan, cycle to work scheme, global bonus plan, share scheme, rewards scheme, life assurance, generous shift allowance and overtime premiums.
Minimum Qualifications
Qualifications and Experience:
• Minimum HNC Electrical/ Mechanical/ Mechatronics.
• Experience working in manufacturing role with an eye for continuous improvement
• Experience in a customer facing role would be desirable
• An understanding of machinery safety and safe working practices.
• Experience in diagnosing faults with an analytical mind
• AutoCAD Electrical or equivalent experience 3D CAD experience is desired
• Good understanding of MS Office applications.
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.
Use of AI Statement
At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Job Title: Instrumentation Engineer (Test & Validation)
Salary: £49,500 - £61,000 depending on skills demonstrated
Contract: Full time & permanent
Location: Desford, Leicestershire
The Opportunity
Looking to apply your instrumentation, testing and data-acquisition expertise to the development and validation of world-class construction equipment? Join our Product Development, Test & Validation team at Caterpillar Desford.
We have an opportunity for an Instrumentation Engineer to join the Product Development, Test & Validation team at Desford. You will provide instrumentation, measurement and data-acquisition expertise, working closely with engineers, technicians and suppliers to deliver safe, accurate and reliable measurement and data-acquisition solutions for machine, component and test-rig validation activities. You will support the full test lifecycle, from defining measurement requirements and selecting sensors through to installation, system configuration, test support, data-quality verification and equipment assurance, helping engineers make confident product decisions and supporting the development of Caterpillar's construction equipment.
What you will do:
As a Instrumentation Engineer, you are accountable for, but not limited to:
• Define instrumentation and data-acquisition requirements with test engineers and product development teams, selecting appropriate sensors, transducers, signal-conditioning equipment, cabling and hardware to provide dependable instrumentation solutions that meet test requirements.
• Plan, install and commission instrumentation systems on construction equipment, test rigs and components, ensuring sensors and cables are safely installed, protected and routed to support safe, efficient and high-quality test execution.
• Configure and verify data-acquisition systems to capture accurate, repeatable and traceable engineering data, including pressure, temperature, force, strain, displacement, acceleration, speed, torque, flow and electrical signals.
• Monitor data quality and resolve technical issues, verifying channel configuration, sensor scaling and sample rates, and identifying measurement, safety and quality risks before they affect test delivery. Diagnose instrumentation, wiring, communication and data-acquisition issues, responding effectively during machine testing.
• Maintain and improve instrumentation equipment and technical records, including calibration status, configuration, condition, availability and obsolescence, helping to improve the standardisation, availability and control of instrumentation equipment.
• Support laboratory quality and continuous improvement, contributing to the effective maintenance of the ISO/IEC 17025 management system, including test-method control, measurement uncertainty, metrological traceability, corrective actions and standard instrumentation practices.
• Build strong working relationships across Product Development and Test & Validation, sharing technical knowledge and providing guidance on instrumentation and data-acquisition equipment.
NB. The panel cannot make assumptions when shortlisting therefore please demonstrate your qualifications and experience on your CV relevant to the criteria outlined.
What You Can Demonstrate:
Level: Working Knowledge
• Technical Excellence: Applies technical knowledge of instrumentation and data-acquisition systems to select, configure, install and maintain appropriate equipment, ensuring reliable solutions and high-quality test data.
• Accuracy and Attention to Detail: Checks and verifies sensor configuration, scaling, sample rates, calibration information and technical records accurately, recognising the impact that errors or omissions can have on measurement validity and test results.
• Troubleshooting Technical Problems: Diagnoses and resolves instrumentation, wiring, communication and data-acquisition issues using systematic troubleshooting methods, helping minimise test disruption and maintain reliable equipment operation.
• Product Testing: Applies appropriate test methods, procedures and equipment when supporting machine, component and test-rig testing, ensuring instrumentation delivers safe, repeatable and dependable test results.
What You May Have:
• Applied technical knowledge of instrumentation, electrical/electronic engineering or a related discipline, sufficient to select and apply appropriate instrumentation and measurement solutions.
• Strong working knowledge of instrumentation, sensors and data-acquisition systems, including the selection, installation, configuration and verification of measurement systems.
• Working knowledge of test and measurement technologies, including data-acquisition and analysis platforms such as Dewesoft, HBK, National Instruments, Vector, ETAS or similar systems, to capture reliable data and diagnose instrumentation or system issues.
• Working understanding of laboratory quality principles, ideally ISO/IEC 17025, to support calibration, traceability and equipment assurance, with awareness of CAN-based vehicle communications, machine-network data acquisition or strain-gauge measurement techniques.
Pending the number of applications, the criteria for the position may be enhanced to facilitate shortlisting.

One Company, Limitless Opportunities
Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives. We do business on every continent, principally operating through three primary segments – Construction Industries, Resource Industries, and Energy & Transportation – and providing financing and related services through our Financial Products segment.
Careers at Caterpillar are limitless, we have opportunities in Engineering, Human Resources, Manufacturing, Marketing, Sales, Supply Chain and so much more. You can create the career you want. It’s your time and talent, make it count.
Our Sustainability Commitment
Caterpillar has a long-standing commitment to sustainability, one of our five Values in Action. It is part of who we are and what we do. We actively lead sustainable green initiatives to preserve the environment, help reduce poverty with the Caterpillar Foundation and stay involved in the communities we help build.

You will act as a responsible designer and intelligent customer, ensuring quality, consistency and technical rigour throughout the project lifecycle.

• Knowledge of relevant earthing and lightning protection codes and standards for the UK and Europe
• Experience developing earthing and lightning protection systems in nuclear or high‑integrity environments

• Understanding of commercial availability and cost considerations for materials

Job Description:
Leonardo offers a range of Apprenticeships across a variety of STEM and business routes, offering paid training, coupled with on the job learning that enables you to gain practical skills, experience and knowledge that sets up the best start to your career. The Apprenticeship:
Our Aerospace Manufacturing Composites apprenticeship is suited for those who are interested in the practical (hands-on) elements of engineering.
Over the 3 years on scheme, you will have the opportunity to rotate across a number of placements, based within the Dynamics Composites Centre (DCC) department, which is the area that manufactures blades for many of the Leonardo Helicopter aircraft, including military, civil and VVIP aircraft. The ultimate aim of the scheme is to move you into a final placement area based on the skills displayed during the apprenticeship.
The apprenticeship will start with an Induction into Leonardo, followed by a Yeovil College Induction to ensure that apprenticeship requirements and expectations are fully established.
You will combine your time between Yeovil College and work placements at Leonardo Helicopters, increasing your work placements as you move through the years.
Throughout the apprenticeship, apprentices may be placed in some or all of the following departmental areas within DCC:
• Clean room: The manufacture of the majority of the blade products is completed in this area (including the blade spar, which is the main structural component of the blade)
• Repairs: The area that deals with the in-service products, the blades come in from working aircraft that require maintenance or repair (this can be from general wear and tear or from battle damage)
• Non Destructive Test (NDT): The testing of the blades through the use of non-destructive test methods is covered in this placement
• Inspection: The Inspection of completed processes/tasks against the requirements of the Leonardo Engineering standards
• DCC Quality Control (QC): This department is responsible for the audit of DCC process compliance, and the Investigation of any product/process non-compliance that may occur.

• Grow your knowledge of an engineering business.
• Develop practical skills in engineering and understanding key processes and technologies.
• Support early careers activities - our apprentices have the opportunity to work as STEM ambassadors in schools, colleges and universities

Job Description:
Manager, Public Interest (PI) Audit
Grant Thornton UK LLP | Audit | Birmingham
Within our Audit practice, we're very keen to support and hire those who have had career breaks or time away from Audit, who would like to return to a busy, flexible auditing role. Our vacancies for qualified Auditors are all open to supporting the up-skilling and re-integration of returners to our business.
A look into the role
The PI Audit Manager owns delivery of audit engagements for our largest and most scrutinised clients, end to end. This is a role with full accountability for audit quality, client relationship management, team leadership and financial performance on each engagement, operating under the heightened regulatory expectations that apply to Public Interest entities. The role also carries a wider responsibility for developing people and building the PI practice across the Birmingham office and the Midlands market.
Here are some things you can expect from this role:
Key Responsibilities
Audit quality and technical delivery
• Owns the design and oversight of audit strategy for each engagement, including risk assessment and materiality, ensuring full compliance with ISAs (UK), the firm's methodology and PI-specific regulatory requirements.
• Takes personal responsibility for the quality of the audit file, exercising sound judgement on complex and contentious areas and escalating to the Engagement Leader only where genuinely needed.
• Leads on enhanced auditor reporting requirements applicable to PIs, including key audit matters and going concern disclosures, and maintains independence and ethical compliance across the portfolio.
Client and stakeholder management
• Acts as the day-to-day point of contact for the client, leading client meetings and presenting audit findings to Audit Committees where appropriate.
• Manages client expectations proactively on timetable, deliverables and fees, so surprises are the exception rather than the norm.
People leadership
• Leads the engagement team day to day, coaching Assistant Managers and Associates in real time and through formal appraisals.
• Acts as people manager and career coach for a number of public interest associates, and contributes to the wider talent and inclusion agenda in the Birmingham office.
Financial and commercial management
• Owns the engagement budget, taking corrective action before overruns occur and leading fee discussions with clients where scope changes arise.
• Identifies opportunities to grow the PI portfolio and the wider Audit practice in the Midlands.
Project management and delivery
• Plans and project manages the full audit cycle, from planning through fieldwork to completion, coordinating specialist input as needed.
• Produces or reviews all client deliverables, including the Audit Plan and Audit Findings Report, to a high technical standard.
Risk, ethics and professional standards
• Adheres to the firm's risk management policies and acts with integrity and in line with the firm's values in all client and internal dealings.
• Maintains professional competence through mandatory training, applied consistently across engagements.
Skills and Attributes for Success
• High-Profile Contact: The day-to-day face of the firm for the client, building trust through technical credibility and leading client meetings, including presenting to Audit Committees where appropriate.
• Leadership Skills: Experience leading an engagement team, coaching Assistant Managers and Associates, and taking full accountability for audit quality and delivery on Public Interest engagements.
• Technical Expertise: Sound technical judgement across ISAs (UK), UK GAAP and IFRS, with the confidence to apply this to complex and contentious audit areas.
Qualifications and Experience
• Fully qualified as a chartered accountant (e.g. ACA, ACCA, CA, ICAS, ICAEW or international equivalent).
• Experience planning, leading and delivering major external audit and assurance engagements in a managerial capacity.
• Proven technical expertise in ISAs (UK), UK GAAP and IFRS, with knowledge of PI-specific regulatory requirements.
Knowing you're right for us
We're interested in professionals with a genuine creative vision and the confidence to make it happen. You can expect plenty of autonomy in this role, so we look for people who will take initiative and seek out opportunities to improve our current relationships and processes. If you're serious about auditing and ready to take on some of our clients' most complex issues, this role is for you.
Knowing we're right for you
Embracing uniqueness, the culture at Grant Thornton thrives on the contributions of all our people, we never settle for what is easy, we look beyond to deliver the right thing, for everyone. Building an inclusive culture, where we value difference and respect our colleagues, helps our people to perform at the best of their ability and realise their potential.
Our open and accessible culture means you'll interact with leaders who are interested in you and everything you bring to our firm. The things that set you apart, we value them. That's why we give you the freedom to bring your whole self to work and pursue your passions inside and outside of work.
Beyond the job
Life is more than work. The things you do, and the people you're with outside of work matter, that's why we're happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles, and we'll always do our best to keep your work and life in balance.
The impact you can make here will go far beyond your day job. From secondments, to fundraising for local charities, or investing in entrepreneurs in the developing world, you'll be giving back to society. It's that drive to do the right thing that runs through our every move, grounded in our firm's values, purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind.
We're looking for people who want to contribute, spark fresh ideas and go beyond expectations. People who want to be able to proudly do what's right, for the firm, our clients, our people and themselves. It's how it should be.

Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.

This long term investment will create skilled jobs and strengthen collaboration with academic, NHS, and government partners. We welcome experts ready to help expand access to life saving vaccines.
At Moderna's Harwell manufacturing facility, you will play a critical role in ensuring the quality, integrity, and stability of materials and products supporting our mRNA manufacturing operations. Reporting to the Associate Director, Quality Control, you will combine hands-on analytical chemistry expertise with the coordination and execution of GMP stability programs, using advanced analytical technologies, laboratory information systems, and scientific data analysis to support manufacturing, product release, and regulatory compliance. This is an opportunity to contribute to global stability programs, strengthen analytical excellence, and explore emerging digital and Generative AI-enabled technologies within a highly regulated, science-driven environment.

• Perform scientific data trending and statistical analysis: Analyse stability testing results to identify trends, evaluate product performance over time, and support scientific assessment of stability data. Maintain up-to-date stability tables, charts, and statistical analyses across ongoing studies, contributing to data-driven quality and regulatory decisions.

Contribute to the preparation and review of stability-related sections for regulatory submissions, ensuring scientific accuracy, data integrity, and alignment with current regulatory requirements.

Share technical knowledge with colleagues and support more junior laboratory staff through data review, training, and troubleshooting activities.

Author and revise SOPs, technical protocols, and reports while identifying opportunities to improve laboratory workflows, analytical reliability, and stability program execution.
• Uphold GMP compliance and data integrity: Execute laboratory and stability activities in accordance with applicable GxP regulations, internal policies, SOPs, and work instructions. Apply Good Documentation Practices and data integrity principles to ensure analytical results, electronic records, and supporting documentation are accurate, complete, traceable, and readily available for regulatory audits and inspections.

Job Description: Equipment Technician Wafer Fab and Epitaxy (Continental Shift)

Our technologies are integral to virtually every type of telecom, enterprise, and data centre network, and support advanced manufacturing and next generation sensing applications. Lumentum’s UK wafer fabrication facility in Caswell is a centre of excellence for high-performance optoelectronic devices used in telecommunications and industrial systems.

As an Equipment Technician, you will provide technical support for the operation and maintenance of wafer fabrication and epitaxy equipment on a continental shift pattern. This role offers the opportunity to work on advanced III-V semiconductor technologies within a highly specialised UK fabrication facility, supporting products deployed globally in next-generation communications networks. Your primary focus will be the fault diagnosis, repair, and optimisation of advanced semiconductor process tools including vacuum, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, and RF systems, as well as equipment handling hazardous process gases and chemicals.

·       Manage chemical and specialty gas supply systems in compliance with statutory, site safety and environmental standards.
·       Support maintenance of gas delivery, exhaust and abatement systems associated with epitaxy and PECVD tools.
·       Manage spare parts inventory to ensure availability of critical components and minimise downtime.
·       Implement and support preventative maintenance strategies to maximise OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) and uptime.
·       Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives (Kaizen, 6S, 8D) and maintain accurate documentation of actions and outcomes.
·       Participate in production and planning meetings to represent equipment engineering performance.
·       Support the site emergency response function including participation in the Site Emergency Response Team.

·       MES (PROMIS) and IT Teams

Veterinary Surgeon
Location: Harlow & Epping, Essex
Hours: Full-time, 40 hours per week – 4-day compressed or 5-day options available

Salary: £66,000–£70,000 per annum DOE
Looking for more than a traditional GP role? Join Forest Vets and work across our established Epping hospital and brand-new Harlow hospital, where you'll have the opportunity to manage complex cases, work with advanced diagnostics, perform surgery every week and collaborate with an experienced team of certificate holders. This is primary care with genuine hospital-level clinical depth.
Why join us?
• Guaranteed surgery time every week, with around 6 surgical cases per day at Epping and growing surgical caseloads at Harlow
• Work in a busy hospital environment managing genuine emergencies including RTAs, GDVs, haem abdomen, blocked bladders, foreign body ingestions, cystotomies and paralysis
• Access to advanced CT, imaging and endoscopy, alongside two theatres at both Harlow and Epping
• Join a highly experienced clinical team with certificate holders in medicine, surgery, cardiology, dermatology and diagnostic imaging
• Work alongside three medicine certificate holders and two imaging certificate holders, with a strong culture of case discussion and clinical collaboration
• Manage your own cases from investigation through to treatment, with most cases worked up in-house
• Dedicated inpatient shift once a week, typically caring for 10–12 hospitalised patients with dedicated nursing support
• Choose between a four-day compressed week or five-day working pattern
• Opportunity to help shape and grow the clinical offering at the brand-new Harlow hospital
• No OOH, with the current weekend rota reducing as the team continues to grow
The Practice & Team
Forest Vets is a busy, clinically progressive practice across Essex, with this role offering the opportunity to work between our established Epping hospital and our brand-new purpose-built Harlow hospital.
Epping is a busy hospital supporting both its own clients and local practices, meaning the team sees a genuine emergency caseload alongside primary care. Cases referred into the hospital include RTAs, GDVs, haemabdomens, blocked bladders, foreign body ingestions, cystotomies and paralysis. The clinical team enjoys the variety and complexity this brings, with a strong focus on working cases up properly rather than automatically referring them elsewhere.
Harlow is our exciting new hospital site and represents a significant investment in the future of Forest Vets. It has five consultation rooms, two theatres, a dedicated dental area and advanced diagnostic facilities including CT, X-ray, imaging and endoscopy. There is also a dedicated cat-only consultation and waiting area, separate dog and cat wards, a six-station preparation room, isolation facilities and an in-house laboratory. The Harlow caseload is continuing to grow, meaning there is genuine scope for you to help shape how busy and clinically ambitious the site becomes.
As a Veterinary Surgeon, you'll receive at least one dedicated surgery day each week. At Epping, this currently averages around six surgical cases per day, while the Harlow surgical caseload continues to develop alongside the new hospital. You'll be expected to be confident with routine soft tissue surgery, with the opportunity to build your surgical experience as the hospital grows.
The role also includes a weekly inpatient shift, where you'll typically manage around 10–12 hospitalised patients with dedicated nursing support. This gives you the opportunity to follow cases beyond the consultation room and develop your skills in ongoing patient management.
You'll be joining a particularly strong clinical team. Across Forest Vets, there are currently certificate holders in medicine, small animal surgery, cardiology, dermatology and diagnostic imaging, including three medicine certificate holders and two imaging certificate holders. This creates an excellent environment for clinical discussion and development. The team has a genuinely collaborative approach to cases, and you'll have plenty of opportunity to discuss challenging patients with colleagues who enjoy getting stuck into a difficult case.
The practice currently refers spinal cases externally and will soon also refer ophthalmology cases while the practice's current ophthalmology certificate holder moves on. Otherwise, there is a strong appetite to work cases up within the practice wherever possible.
We're looking for an experienced Veterinary Surgeon who is comfortable in a hospital environment and can confidently manage their own cases. Around five years' experience would be a guide, although this will depend on the individual's previous exposure and level of clinical confidence. Previous hospital experience is essential, as is confidence with basic soft tissue surgery, ECC presentations, hospitalised patients and sole-charge decision making.
You'll also need to be empathetic. This is a busy hospital environment and you'll encounter some genuinely difficult and sensitive cases. We're looking for someone who cares deeply about their patients and clients but who also has the resilience to remain calm, compassionate and clinically focused when cases become challenging.
For those looking for flexibility, there are two working patterns available. You can choose a four-day compressed week, working three 11-hour days from 8am–7pm plus one shorter day from 8am–4.30pm, giving you one additional day off each week. Alternatively, you can work five 8-hour days, with a mixture of 8am–4.30pm and 11am–7pm shifts. Lunch breaks are one hour on longer days and 30 minutes on five-day patterns, with admin time built into the working day.

Ideally around 5 years' UK experience, depending on previous clinical exposure

Previous hospital experience is essential

Confident with routine soft tissue surgery
•
Comfortable managing genuine emergency and critical cases

Confident managing hospitalised patients independently

Comfortable making clinical decisions in sole charge

Strong clinical reasoning and diagnostic skills
•
Previous referral experience would be advantageous

An empathetic and compassionate approach to clients dealing with difficult or sensitive cases
•
Resilient, calm and able to thrive in a busy, fast-paced hospital environment
•
A collaborative approach and enthusiasm for discussing cases with colleagues
• Someone who wants to develop their clinical skills and contribute to the continued growth of the Harlow hospital
